Create "Fog system" plan in docs/plans/p102_fog-system.md

Category: Fog

Create a fog system for Aekasha. The debugger drawer should have its own  Fog system tab (design an icon for this) and each fog setup should be scene specific. It should be toggleable on/off (the whole system) and it should have at least three different fog passes available to choose from (or notify if some of these should not be implemented, or something else would be beneficial for Aekasha):
- Basic Three.js fog (simple fog)
- Three.js FogExp2
- Global volumetric fog (or something like it)
Also all the parameters for the fog should be editable in the debugger drawer. It can be defined in its own file: myScene.fog.json.

Context from the removed sky box plans (p110-p115; full texts in git history): fog coupling with the sky box was an explicit non-goal of the sky box epic, so it is open for this plan. The sky box's `ground` layer already has `useAtmosphereHorizon` (blends toward the atmosphere's horizon colour, a form of aerial perspective), and the day-night cycle changes the horizon colour over time, so consider a fog colour that can follow the active sky box. Screen-space passes belong in the PostFX chain (`core/PostFX.ts`). Headless WebGPU doesn't render under WSL2, so visual checks need a real browser.

If for some reason this plan can't or shouldn't be created with this specification or has some high risks of failing the implementation, notify immediately. You are allowed to change the naming of the plan or the header information if they are not well described, but please notify about this.

UNDER_CONSTRUCTION
Create "Statistics Profiler mega window" plan in docs/plans/p220_stats-profiler-mega-window.md

Category: Statistics should have its own window that would display far more deeper real-time info about the scene and the current state. This will be the base ticket for more plans in the future and we will not implement everything in this plan. The window should have similar tabs as the debugger drawer (can have the same style). In this plan we should implement these tabs:
- Overview (this should be like the main icon for the stats window, design this)
- Objects (this can be an isometric wireframe cubes, design this)
- Settings (a cog wheel, design this if it doesn't exist)

The window can be opened either by clicking the on screen stats panels, with a button from the Stats debugger tab, and from the top on screen tools (add the spedometer icon button next to the pause button). All of these functionalities need to implemented. Also add an option to the Stats debugger tab to whether to enable/disable the Profiler mega window opening by clicking the on screen stats panels: "Profiler mega window can be opened by clicking the on screen stats panels" (default true).

The Overview tab will have some key data on it like TFPS (true FPS, meaning how many frames in would show per second without the vsync/restricter), FPS, CPU, Physics calculation + transfer (for Worker thread) ms per frame, memory consumed, total amount of entities, total amount of meshes, total amount of triangles, total amount vertices, and what else (you may suggest some key measurments)? Not sure if it is possible but the total amounts should only count the entities/meshes/objects/triangles/vertices that are visible/enabled (not culled). This view should update at a requested rate (configured in the Settings tab). This tab has no graphs.

The Objects tab should do a breakdown of the different entity, mesh, triangle, vertices (etc.) counts. This view can have graphs, but I am not sure yet how to display them (you can suggest what to use here).

TODO_SETTINGS_TAB_PLAN

Context from removed _DONE_ plans (p027, p070/p071, p140, p142; full texts in git history):
- Existing opt-in stats sources to read rather than re-measure: physics step time and the worker messaging latency (`getLastPhysicsStepDuration`, `getLastPhysicsStepMessagingLatency` in `core/PhysicsAPI.ts`, gated by `AppConfig.physics.stepStatsEnabled`, default off; dispatch and write-back are kept separate from the step time and never summed, and `writeBackMs` means different things on `MESSAGE_BATCH` vs `SHARED_MEMORY`, so label it), Three.js ray stats (`getRayCastStats`, `core/Raycast.ts`), physics ray stats (`getPhysicsRayStats`, `core/PhysicsAPI.ts`), PostFX per-pass GPU timings (`getPostFxPassStats`, `debug/PostFXProfiler.ts`, console-only today) and the sky box bake stats (`core/Debug/SkyBox/_dbg__BakeStats.ts`, GPU timer `_dbg__GPUTimer.ts`, WebGPU only). The shared windowed-counter util is `utils/stats/IntervalCounterStats.ts`.
- p140 proposed introducing a generic `registerStatsSource(id, getter)` registry here if the profiler needs to enumerate sources.
- Every stats source is opt-in so it costs nothing when off; keep that for whatever the profiler turns on (enable while the window is open).

[NOTE: This should be implemented after the Profiler mega window and IS NOT A PLAN, just run it]
Add two more options to the Stats debugger tab (after Enable measuring option) and in the Debug Tools Controls tab's Production test mode folder:
- Enable measuring display panels in prodTest (checkbox)
- Enable Profiler mega window in prodTest (checkbox)
If the measuring display panels option is true, then the panels will show in prodTest (when the onScreenTool play button is pressed). If the Profiler mega window option is true then the the mega window can be displayed in prodTest by clicking the on screen stats panels (if that feature is turned on and there is at least one panel shown), from the top on screen tools (next to the pause button), or then by having the Profiler mega window already open when the prodTest play button is pressed.
